_comment: 15-field form (version 3, dataset branch): the problem statement's 10 fields of version 2, unchanged, plus 5 industry-standard context fields (g, c, k, h, n), all optional. Definitions and sources: eval/nlu15/LABELING_15.md. The app still uses schema/incident_form.json (10 fields); this file is for the 15-field dataset.

fields.name: incident_type
fields.ask: What kind of incident was it?

fields.name: severity
fields.ask: How serious is it: low, medium, high or critical?

fields.name: date_time
fields.normalize: code resolves relative phrases ('around 10 AM', 'yesterday evening') against the device clock

fields.name: equipment_involved
fields.ask: Was any equipment or asset involved?

fields.name: description
fields.source: the user's own words; not generated by the model

fields.name: immediate_actions
fields.ask: Has anything been done about it yet?

fields.name: task
fields.ask: What were they doing just before it happened?
fields.standard: OSHA Form 301 item 14: what the employee was doing just before the incident

fields.name: immediate_cause
fields.ask: Do you know what caused it?
fields.standard: Factories Act 1948 Form 18 (cause of accident); incident investigation: immediate cause

fields.name: property_damage
fields.ask: Was any property or equipment damaged?
fields.standard: incident reporting of property and equipment damage (ISO 45001 incidents include property damage)

fields.name: hazard_status
fields.ask: Is the hazard under control now?
fields.standard: incident forms: area made safe / hazard contained

fields.name: reported_to
fields.standard: Factories Act 1948 s.88 notice of accidents; internal EHS escalation

fields.name: follow_up
fields.source: picked by code from data/followup_catalogue.json for the incident type; editable at review

tools.name: update_report
tools.args: any subset of the keyed fields above; only fields the user actually stated

tools.name: submit_report
tools.args: none; code refuses it while a mandatory field is empty

tools.name: no_op
tools.args: none; the utterance held nothing for the form
